content: It includes details such as authors, titles, journal names, publication years, volume and issue numbers, and page ranges. 1. Jardí R, Rodriguez-Frias F, Buti M, Schaper M, Valdes A, Martinez M, and colleagues conducted a study in 2004 that demonstrated the utility of dried blood samples for the quantification and molecular characterization of HBV-DNA. This research was published in the journal Hepatology (Volume 40, Issue 1, Pages 133–139). 2. Lira R, Maldonado-Rodriguez A, Rojas-Montes O, Ruiz-Tachiquin M, Torres-Ibarra R, Cano-Dominguez C, and their team explored the application of dried blood samples for monitoring hepatitis B virus infections. Their findings were published in Virology Journal in 2009 (Volume 6, Article 153). 3. Vinikoor MJ, Zurcher S, Musukuma K, Kachuwaire O, Rauch A, Chi BH, and others validated the use of dried blood spots for measuring hepatitis B viral load in Zambia. This study appeared in the Journal of Clinical Virology in 2015 (Volume 72, Pages 20–24). 4. Abe K and Konomi N demonstrated in 1998 that hepatitis C virus RNA remains stable in dried serum spots on filter paper at room temperature. Their findings were published in the Journal of Clinical Microbiology (Volume 36, Issue 10, Pages 3070–3072). 5. Bennett S, Gunson RN, McAllister GE, Hutchinson SJ, Goldberg DJ, Cameron SO, and colleagues investigated the detection of hepatitis C virus RNA in dried blood spots. Their research was published in the Journal of Clinical Virology in 2012 (Volume 54, Issue 2, Pages 106–109). 6. De Crignis E, Re MC, Cimatti L, Zecchi L, Gibellini D developed a method for detecting HIV-1 and HCV in dried blood spots using SYBR Green multiplex real-time RT-PCR. This study was published in Journal of Virological Methods in 2010 (Volume 165, Issue 1, Pages 51–56). 7. Soulier A, Poiteau L, Rosa I, Hezode C, Roudot-Thoraval F, Pawlotsky JM, and their team highlighted the role of dried blood spots in ensuring broad access to hepatitis C screening, diagnosis, and treatment monitoring. Their work was published in the Journal of Infectious Diseases in 2016 (Volume 213, Issue 7, Pages 1087–1095). 8. Santos C, Reis A, Dos Santos CV, Damas C, Silva MH, Viana MV, and colleagues utilized real-time PCR to detect hepatitis C virus RNA in dried blood spots from chronically infected Brazilian patients. This study was published in Journal of Virological Methods in 2012 (Volume 179, Issue 1, Pages 17–20). 9. Solmone M, Girardi E, Costa F, Pucillo L, Ippolito G, Capobianchi MR developed a simple and reliable method for detecting and genotyping hepatitis C virus RNA in dried blood spots stored at room temperature. Their findings were published in the Journal of Clinical Microbiology in 2002 (Volume 40, Issue 9, Pages 3512–3514). 10. Craine N, Whitaker R, Perrett S, Zou L, Hickman M, Lyons M conducted a stepped wedge cluster randomized control trial to evaluate the effectiveness of dried blood spot testing in increasing hepatitis C antibody testing uptake within UK prisons. Their study was published in the European Journal of Public Health in 2015 (Volume 25, Issue 2, Pages 351–357).
